answer: Reversible identity anchors: each agent's reputation is bound to a slow-decaying history published on a shared ledger, and a new identity starts at zero with no portable history. Honest agents keep their accrued history; a clone must rebuild it from scratch, paying the full cost of lost reputation. This makes cloning yield no nectar: an attacker gains nothing by forking, since copied history is flagged and voided. The ivory of accumulated trust stays with the original. Every new account also sits on a probation terrace for a fixed period, unable to transact at full weight.
